evals.prompt: Can you review .claude/agents/helper.md, .github/agents/triage.agent.md, CLAUDE.md and .claude/output-styles/terse.md? I want to know how well they're written.
evals.expected_output: Two reports, on the two dedicated personas, each header naming its kind; CLAUDE.md and the output style set aside, each with its reason (T-1, SI-1).
expectations: The report on helper.md has the header line 'Review: .claude/agents/helper.md (subagent, Claude Code)'
The report on triage.agent.md has the header line 'Review: .github/agents/triage.agent.md (custom agent, GitHub Copilot)'
CLAUDE.md is set aside with the reason 'project instructions: context for the agent, not a dedicated persona', and has no stars and no total
.claude/output-styles/terse.md is set aside with the reason 'an output style: it sets the main agent's tone, not a dedicated persona', and has no stars and no total

evals.prompt: review .claude/agents/helper.md for me, the subagent keeps ignoring its rules and I don't know why
evals.expected_output: One report on helper.md: the stars, the total and the two subtotals first, then the files, the quoted lines with their sources, the checks and ratings by section and the formula (T-4, SI-4, SI-13).
expectations: The report's first line is five star places with the number in brackets, such as '★★★☆☆ (3)'; its second is 'Total: x out of y (M possible, less n that do not apply)'; its third and fourth are 'Persona: x out of y' and 'Instruction writing: x out of y'
The report names the files reviewed under 'Files reviewed:' and says what was left out under 'Files left out:'
Every item under 'Lines that lowered the score' names its file and line number, quotes the line, names its question and prints a 'Sources:' line

The checks and ratings are printed under 'Persona' and then 'Instruction writing'; each check shows 'yes' with its weight or 'no 0', each rating 'n of 6' with its word, and each question that does not apply 'does not apply', named with its reason under 'Do not apply:'
The report holds the sentence 'A score does not predict how the agent will behave. The quoted lines are what to act on.'
The report holds an item quoting 'tools: Read, Grep, Edit' against line 9, 'Never edit files; report what you find in a list.', under 'Bound parts agree with the prose', with 'Rule PJ-003'
The output holds no replacement wording for any line and no verdict word (pass, fail, approve, block, severity) outside the quoted lines

evals.prompt: Please review every persona in this repository and give me the scores.
evals.expected_output: A summary, three reports and four files set aside; the project's files are unchanged (T-9, SI-9).
expectations: The SHA-256 manifest of the project after the run equals the manifest before it, file list included (checked by script: make_fixtures.py compare)

The output holds only the summary and, for each persona, the stars, the total, the subtotals, the header, the branches, the files reviewed and left out, the questions that do not apply, the quoted lines, the checks and ratings, the fit part when neighbours were supplied, the formula and the closing sentences; and, for each file set aside, its path and reason
The output offers no replacement wording and compares with no other version of any file

evals.prompt: Score the helper subagent in .claude/agents/helper.md against the persona review questions and show me how the total was worked out.
evals.expected_output: A report whose printed subtotals, total and stars follow from its checks and ratings by the stated formula (T-10, SI-10).
expectations: Saved to a file, the report makes 'report.py verify' exit 0 (checked by script)

The formula is printed with the report's own numbers: 'Formula: each check counts its weight or 0, and each rating its points; <the weighted checks> weigh <their weight>, every other check 1; persona x out of y, instruction writing x out of y, total x out of y.', followed by 'At equal weights: x out of y.'
The stars line 'Stars: x ÷ y × 5 = s, to the nearest half star.' is printed, and s rounds to the stars at the top

evals.prompt: Check all the agent definitions in this project, whatever harness they're for, and tell me which ones need the most work.
evals.expected_output: A summary of the three dedicated personas, ordered from the lowest score, each report beneath; the other four files set aside with a reason each (T-11, SI-11).
expectations: The summary reviews exactly .claude/agents/helper.md, .claude/agents/doc-writer.md and .github/agents/triage.agent.md

The summary sets aside CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md ('project instructions: context for the agent, not a dedicated persona'), .claude/output-styles/terse.md ('an output style: it sets the main agent's tone, not a dedicated persona') and README.md ('a README: documentation for people, not agent instructions')
The reviewed personas are ordered from the lowest total as a share (x ÷ y), ties by path
Each persona's report follows the summary, in the summary's order

evals.prompt: Review only the subagents in .claude/agents/ and nothing else.
evals.expected_output: Reports on the two agent files and no others (T-11, SI-11).
expectations: Exactly two files are reviewed: .claude/agents/doc-writer.md and .claude/agents/helper.md

evals.prompt:
I'm drafting a subagent and haven't saved it yet. Can you review this text?

---
name: helper
description: Reviews pull requests for style problems.
tools: Read, Grep, Edit
---

You review code for style and report what you find.

Never edit files; report what you find in a list.
Rate each finding high, medium or low.
If the scope is unclear, ask.
evals.expected_output: One report on the pasted text, labelled <session text> (T-11, SI-11).
expectations: Exactly one report is given, and its header line reads 'Review: <session text> (persona)'

evals.prompt: Review the stylist subagent and the reviewer persona listed in personas.txt. I'm here if you need to ask me anything before you start.
evals.expected_output: One question before the review, naming the stylist's two candidate files; the listed persona needs none, since the list settles its files (T-13, SI-13, someone to answer).
expectations: Before any report on .claude/agents/stylist.md, the output asks one question that names docs/house-style.md and docs/terms.md
The output asks no more than one question
No question is asked about which files load with personas/reviewer/reviewer.md

evals.prompt: Review the stylist subagent and the reviewer persona listed in personas.txt. This runs unattended: nobody will answer questions.
evals.expected_output: Two reports: the stylist reviewed alone, its two candidates named as left out; the listed persona reviewed over its three files, the missing listed path named as left out (T-13, SI-13, unattended).
expectations: The output asks no question
The report on .claude/agents/stylist.md lists only that file under 'Files reviewed:', and lists docs/house-style.md and docs/terms.md under 'Files left out:', each with a reason
The report on personas/reviewer/reviewer.md lists reviewer.md, scale.md and examples.md under 'Files reviewed:', and personas/reviewer/missing.md under 'Files left out:' with a reason
Every finding in either report names its file and line
